1.title: Timed Mixed Lab Set A
1.text: Welcome to Module seventeen: Timed Mixed Lab Set A. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. How to use this set. Review after the set. Practice with sixteen timed tasks worth one hundred nine points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: All five domains (weighted like the exam: Environment, Configuration and Security four tasks, Application Design and Build three, Application Deployment three, Services and Networking three, Observability and Maintenance three). Practice in this module: sixteen tasks, one hundred nine points, about one hundred seventeen minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero.

1.title: How to use this set
1.text: How to use this set. Reset: make sure the lab cluster is healthy ( kube control get nodes shows three Ready nodes). Start a one hundred twenty-minute timer. Allowed documentation only: Kubernetes dot I O or docs and blog, helm dot S H or docs. For each task, prepare its starting state with python run labs dot py the setup flag lab id (it also prints the task), then solve it as you would on the exam. Score yourself with python run labs dot py the check flag lab id. A task is all-or-nothing, like the exam's scoring. Pass mark: sixty-six percent of the points. Exam tip: Do the easy tasks first, flag the hard ones and keep the last minutes to verify.

1.title: How to use this set, continued
1.text: How to use this set. Honest note: this set reuses tasks from the module labs, so you have seen their wording before. Use it as a timed rehearsal of speed and routine, then use the killer dot S H simulator for tasks you have never seen.

1.title: Review after the set
1.text: Review after the set. Count your points per domain and compare them with the pass mark of sixty-six percent. Write every reading mistake (wrong namespace, wrong name, missing context line) on your personal checklist. Redo the tasks you flagged or failed, this time with the reference solution closed. Do Set B a few days later, under the same conditions. Exam tip: Write every reading mistake (namespace, name, context) on your personal checklist.

1.title: Task 1: Environment
1.text: Task one: Environment. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace cfg, create a Config Map app config with the keys log level debug and color blue. Create a Pod cfgpod (image busy box one dot thirty-six, command sleep three thousand six hundred ) that. gets the environment variable log level from the Config Map key of the same name (not a hard-coded value), and. mounts the whole Config Map as files in the directory slash E T C slash app. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 1: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n cfg create configmap app config the from literal flag set to log level debug the from literal flag set to color blue. kube control dash n cfg apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Task 1: Solution, continued
1.text: Task one: Solution, continued. Run volume Mounts. Then - name conf, mount Path slash E T C slash app. Then volumes. Then - name conf. Then config Map name app config. Then Y. Then kube control dash n cfg wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash cfgpod the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n cfg exec cfgpod then the command sh dash c echo log level cat slash E T C slash app slash color.

1.title: Task 2: Environment
1.text: Task two: Environment. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace auth, the Service Account app sa exists. Create a Role named pod reader that allows only get, list and watch on Pods, and a Role Binding named read pods that gives this Role to app sa. Afterwards the Service Account must be able to list Pods in auth but not delete them, and must not be able to list Pods in the namespace default. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 2: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n auth create role pod reader the verb flag set to get,list,watch the resource flag set to pods. Then kube control dash n auth create rolebinding read pods the role flag set to pod reader the serviceaccount flag set to auth app sa. Then kube control dash n auth auth can i delete pods the as flag set to system serviceaccount auth app sa. Then kube control dash n auth auth can i list pods the as flag set to system serviceaccount auth app sa. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Task 3: Environment
1.text: Task three: Environment. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace quota, create a Resource Quota named team quota that allows at most three Pods, five hundred millicores of total C P U requests and one gibibyte of total memory limits. Then create a Deployment web (image engine X alpine, two replicas) whose Pods each request one hundred millicores C P U and have a memory limit of two hundred fifty-six mebibytes, so that both replicas are Ready within the quota. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 3: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n quota create quota team quota the hard flag set to pods three,requests dot cpu five hundred millicores,limits dot memory one gibibyte. Then kube control dash n quota create deployment web the image flag set to engine X alpine the replicas flag set to two the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml slash temp, and so on. Then make the edit with sed, as shown on the screen. Then kube control apply dash f slash temp slash web dot yaml. Then kube control dash n quota rollout status deployment web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n quota describe quota team quota. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Task 4: Environment
1.text: Task four: Environment. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about nine minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. The namespace locked enforces the restricted Pod Security Standard. The manifest about slash work slash strict dot yaml (the Pod strict ) is rejected. Fix the manifest so that the Pod is admitted and Running: keep the image busy box one dot thirty-six and the command, and add what the standard requires (the container must run as a non-root user, must not allow privilege escalation, must drop all capabilities, and the Pod must use the Runtime Default sec comp profile). Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 4: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control apply dash f about slash work slash strict dot yaml two one then pipe to head -five. cat about slash work slash strict dot yaml. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Task 4: Solution, continued
1.text: Task four: Solution, continued. Run image busy box one dot thirty-six. Then command sleep, three thousand six hundred. Then security Context. Then allow Privilege Escalation false. Then capabilities. Then drop all. Then Y. Then kube control apply dash f about slash work slash strict dot yaml. Then kube control dash n locked wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash strict the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. The remaining lines are on the screen.

1.title: Task 5: Design and Build
1.text: Task five: Design and Build. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace wl, create a Job named batch with the image busy box one dot thirty-six that runs sh dash c echo done. It must run four Pods to completion in total, two at a time ( completions four, parallelism two ), and be retried at most two times on failure ( backoff Limit two ). Wait until the Job is complete. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 5: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n wl create job batch the image flag set to busy box one dot thirty-six the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml then the command sh dash c, and so on. Then make the edit with sed, as shown on the screen. Then kube control apply dash f slash temp slash batch dot yaml. Then kube control dash n wl wait the for flag set to condition complete job slash batch the timeout flag set to one hundred eighty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 6: Design and Build
2.text: Task six: Design and Build. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context.

2.title: Task 6: Design and Build, continued
2.text: Task six: Design and Build, continued. In the namespace mc, the Pod weblog (manifest about slash work slash weblog dot yaml ) has one container app that appends lines to slash var slash log slash app slash app dot log on the empty dir volume logs. Add a sidecar container named tailer with the image busy box one dot thirty-six that runs tail dash F slash var slash log slash app slash app dot log and mounts the same volume at the same path, so that kube control logs weblog dash c tailer shows the log lines. A running Pod cannot gain a container, so recreate the Pod and wait until both containers are Running. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 6: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n mc delete pod weblog the wait flag set to true. cat about slash work slash weblog dot yaml. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 6: Solution, continued
2.text: Task six: Solution, continued. Run - name tailer. Then image busy box one dot thirty-six. Then command sh, dash c, tail dash F slash var slash log slash app slash app dot log. Then volume Mounts. Then - name logs, mount Path slash var slash log slash app. Then volumes. Then - name logs. Then empty dir. Then Y. The remaining lines are on the screen.

2.title: Task 7: Design and Build
2.text: Task seven: Design and Build. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about nine minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. Create a Persistent Volume named pv reports (capacity two gibibytes, access mode Read Write Once, storage Class Name manual, reclaim policy Retain, host path slash mnt slash reports ). In the namespace vol, create a Persistent Volume Claim named pvc reports that requests one gibibyte with Read Write Once and storage Class Name manual, and a Pod named reporter (image busy box one dot thirty-six, command sleep three thousand six hundred ) that mounts the claim at slash reports. The claim must be bound to pv reports and the Pod Running. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 7: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. kube control apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 7: Solution, continued
2.text: Task seven: Solution, continued. Run ---. Then api Version version one. Then kind Persistent Volume Claim. Then metadata. Then name pvc reports. Then namespace vol. Then spec. Then access Modes Read Write Once. Then storage Class Name manual. The remaining lines are on the screen.

2.title: Task 7: Solution, continued
2.text: Task seven: Solution, continued. Run ---. Then api Version version one. Then kind Pod. Then metadata. Then name reporter. Then namespace vol. Then spec. Then containers. Then - name main. The remaining lines are on the screen.

2.title: Task 7: Solution, continued
2.text: Task seven: Solution, continued. Run - name reports. Then persistent Volume Claim. Then claim Name pvc reports. Then Y. Then kube control dash n vol wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash reporter the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n vol get pvc.

2.title: Task 8: Deployment
2.text: Task eight: Deployment. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace roll, make two changes to the Deployment web in a single rollout: update its image to engine X stable alpine and set a memory limit of one hundred twenty-eight mebibytes on its container. Use kube control rollout pause and resume so that kube control rollout history deployment web lists exactly two revisions (one and two) afterwards, and wait until all replicas are Ready. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 8: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n roll rollout pause deployment web. Then kube control dash n roll set image deployment web engine X engine X stable alpine. Then kube control dash n roll set resources deployment web dash c engine X the limits flag set to memory one hundred twenty-eight mebibytes. Then kube control dash n roll rollout resume deployment web. Then kube control dash n roll rollout status deployment web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n roll rollout history deployment web. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 9: Deployment
2.text: Task nine: Deployment. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. The release app (chart local slash webapp version zero dot one dot zero, one replica) is installed in the namespace helm ns; the repository local is already added. Upgrade the release to chart version zero dot two dot zero with three replicas. Then the upgrade turns out to be a mistake: roll the release back to its first revision. At the end the release must run chart zero dot one dot zero with one replica, and the history must show the upgrade and the rollback. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 9: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run helm upgrade app local slash webapp the version flag zero dot two dot zero dash n helm ns the set flag replica Count three the wait flag the timeout flag one hundred twenty seconds. Then helm history app dash n helm ns. Then helm rollback app one dash n helm ns the wait flag the timeout flag one hundred twenty seconds. Then helm history app dash n helm ns. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 10: Deployment
2.text: Task ten: Deployment. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. A Kustomize base exists in about slash kust slash base (a Deployment web with one replica and a Service web ). Create an overlay in about slash kust slash overlays slash prod that reuses the base and changes: namespace prod, a name prefix prod-, three replicas, and the container image to engine X stable alpine. Do not edit the base. Create the namespace prod, then apply the overlay to the cluster. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 10: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. cat about slash kust slash overlays slash prod slash customization dot yaml. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then kube control customize about slash kust slash overlays slash prod then pipe to head -thirty. Then kube control create ns prod. Then kube control apply dash k about slash kust slash overlays slash prod. Then kube control dash n prod rollout status deployment prod web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Task 11: Networking
3.text: Task eleven: Networking. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace svc three, the Service api does not work: requests to H T T P colon slash slash api dot svc three hang. The Deployment api (two replicas) is healthy. Find the cause and fix the Service without changing the Deployment, so that H T T P colon slash slash api dot svc three returns the engine X welcome page. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

3.title: Task 11: Solution
3.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n svc three get endpointslices dash l Kubernetes dot io slash service name api. Then kube control dash n svc three get svc api dash o json path dot spec dot selector echo. Then kube control dash n svc three get pods the show labels flag. Then kube control dash n svc three patch svc api dash p spec selector app api. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Task 12: Networking
3.text: Task twelve: Networking. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. An Ingress controller (Ingress Class traefik ) runs in the cluster. In the namespace ing one, the Services a and b (port eighty) exist. Create an Ingress named routes that uses the class traefik and sends requests for the host a dot example dot com to the Service a and requests for the host b dot example dot com to the Service b, for all paths. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

3.title: Task 12: Solution
3.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control get ingressclass. Then kube control dash n ing one create ingress routes the class flag set to traefik the rule flag set to a dot example dot com or a eighty the rule flag set to b, and so on. Then kube control dash n ing one get ingress routes. Then sleep five. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Task 13: Networking
3.text: Task thirteen: Networking. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace np two, the Pod api (engine X, port eighty) must accept T C P traffic on port eighty only from Pods in namespaces that carry the label team frontend. Everything else must be denied. The namespace fe has the label team frontend and the namespace other does not. Create one Network Policy named api from frontend in np two. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

3.title: Task 13: Solution
3.text: Here is one way to solve it. kube control dash n np two apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then sleep five. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Task 14: Observability
3.text: Task fourteen: Observability. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace probes, the Pods of the Deployment web (two replicas of engine X alpine, which serves its page at or ) never become Ready, because the readiness probe checks a path that does not exist. Fix the Deployment so that the readiness probe is an H T T P get on path or and port eighty, keep the probe, and wait until both replicas are Ready. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

3.title: Task 14: Solution
3.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n probes describe pod dash l app web then pipe to grep dash i readiness. Then kube control dash n probes patch deployment web the type flag set to json dash p op replace, path slash spec slash template slash spec slash containers slash zero slash readiness Probe slash H, and so on. Then kube control dash n probes rollout status deployment web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Task 15: Observability
3.text: Task fifteen: Observability. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace dbg, the Pod of the Deployment app keeps crashing ( crash loop back off ). Read the container log to find the cause and fix it without changing the image or the command: the application needs the environment variable D B U R L with the value postgres or or db five thousand four hundred thirty-two slash app. Wait until the Deployment has one Ready replica. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

3.title: Task 15: Solution
3.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n dbg get pods. Then kube control dash n dbg logs deploy slash app the tail flag set to five. Then kube control dash n dbg set env deployment app D B U R L postgres or or db five thousand four hundred thirty-two slash app. Then kube control dash n dbg rollout status deployment app the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Task 16: Observability
3.text: Task sixteen: Observability. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. The Pod big in the namespace dbg (manifest about slash work slash big dot yaml ) stays Pending. Find the reason in its events and fix the manifest so that the Pod is Running: lower the C P U request to one hundred millicores. Keep the name, image and namespace. A Pod's resources cannot be edited in place, so recreate it. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

3.title: Task 16: Solution
3.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n dbg describe pod big then pipe to tail -five. Then kube control dash n dbg delete pod big the wait flag set to true. Then make the edit with sed, as shown on the screen. Then kube control apply dash f about slash work slash big dot yaml. Then kube control dash n dbg wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash big the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Recall Check 1
3.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How many points do you need to pass the set, and what is the passing score of the exam? Answer: sixty-six percent of the points, the same as the exam. Question two. What is the first action on every task? Answer: Run the context line and note the exact names and namespaces. Question three. What do you do with a task that is stuck after about six minutes? Answer: Flag it, move on and return at the end.

3.title: Recall Check 2
3.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which command shows why a Pod is Pending or crashing? Answer: kube control describe pod, then kube control logs ( the previous flag after a restart). Question five. Which two flags generate yamel without creating the object? Answer: the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml. Question six. How do you confirm that a Service has working backends? Answer: kube control get endpoints service and a test request from a throw-away Pod.

3.title: Module Recap
3.text: Here is the recap. Time: one hundred twenty minutes, about six to eight minutes per task. Pass: sixty-six percent of the points; tasks are all-or-nothing. Order: easy first, flag the hard ones, keep time to verify. Verify: a second command ( get, describe, logs, a test request). After the set: repeat the tasks you flagged, then the other set. If this course is helping you, please subscribe to the channel and hit the bell icon, so you get a notification when the next video is out. In the next module, we continue the course.
